evidence.quote: Using the CASSIS[^1] line analysis software and assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and optically thin lines, a synthetic spectrum is produced for each identified species.
The peak continuum emission is 29 mJy beam$^{-1}$ (5.7 K at 247 GHz)
A total of 354 lines are identified towards AFGL 4176 with a signal-to-noise ratio of three or above.
The column density upper limit is $\leq$1.1$\times$10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$, equivalent to $\leq$0.2% with respect to methanol.
On average, the column density ratios derived for O-bearing species are a factor of three higher than those derived for N-bearing species.
These are found to be $\sim$16 and $\sim$34, respectively.

claims.hypothesis: Does the O/N-bearing ratio indicate the evolutionary stage of AFGL 4176?
claims.experiment: LTE fits of 23 species and ratios to CH3OH
claims.result: O-bearing ratios are a factor of three higher than N-bearing
claims.finding: AFGL 4176 may be a relatively young source

evidence.quote: This may indicate that AFGL 4176 is a relatively young source since nitrogen chemistry generally takes longer to evolve in the gas-phase.

claims.hypothesis: Is AFGL 4176 more similar chemically to low-mass IRAS 16293B or to Galactic centre hot cores?
claims.result: Many O-bearing species within a factor of two of IRAS 16293B; Sgr B2 higher by up to an order of magnitude or more
claims.finding: Composition resembles IRAS 16293B, suggesting complex chemistry set in the cold cloud stage

evidence.quote: the composition of AFGL 4176 more closely resembles that of the low-mass protostar IRAS 16293–2422B than that of high-mass star-forming regions located near the Galactic centre

claims.hypothesis: Do the Garrod 2013 models reproduce the observed abundances?
claims.result: Matches CH3CHO, C2H5OH, CH3OCH3; underpredicts CH3COCH3 and (CH2OH)2; N-bearing off by ~10x except C2H3CN

evidence.quote: the abundances of CH$_3$COCH$_3$ and (CH$_2$OH)$_2$ are underpredicted by at least an order of magnitude
